purpose: Verify (not infer) that the cassette cache-miss found in eval/test_quality_regression.py is caused by the classifier's changed output specifically, not an unrelated break.

issue.title: Fix disposed SCM source control retention

conclusion: Confirmed: the classifier's genuinely different top-3 predictions and confidences (both label order and values changed) are embedded verbatim into the LLM prompt text (triage_prompt.py), which changes LLMCache.compute_key's SHA-256 hash of the full messages payload. The recorded cassette was built against the OLD model's output (its key IS in the cassette); the NEW model's output produces a different key (NOT in the cassette) -- a legitimate cache miss caused by the classifier swap, not an unrelated break. Fix: re-record via .github/workflows/record-cassette.yml (dedicated manual workflow, live Groq calls, already built for this exact scenario).
